page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The system configuration includes 2 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, paired with 8.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a ratio of 4.0 GB memory per vCPU. The CPU cache architecture comprises 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Supported hardware features include AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, FMA, and standard AVX extensions. The instance does not include bundled local SSD storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage for persistent volumes.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded CPU processing alongside standard entry-level multi-threaded metrics. The instance achieved a single-core stress-ng score of 2,692.58, placing it in the top quartile of tested machines, while multi-core stress-ng reached 5,335.58. Geekbench tests yielded a single-core score of 1,502.0 and a multi-core score of 2,729.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks recorded 35.65 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 22.54 GB/sec for large-block writes. In application-specific workloads, static web serving throughput measured 3.36 GB/sec, Redis SET performance reached 3.7 million operations per second, and small 135M LLM model text generation achieved 137.32 tokens per second. The instance provides dedicated core compute efficiency for light workloads that do not require high memory throughput.

The t2d-standard-2 instance is suitable for entry-level microservices, lightweight web servers, basic API endpoints, and low-concurrency background jobs. Its strong single-core performance benefits lightweight text processing and execution tasks, while the core count and memory capacity limit suitability for memory-intensive databases or parallel compute operations.
